supersedes: reports/step17_t5_language/scope_spec.json (language_scope.zh.v1; kept unchanged together with offline_check.json and execution_records.json)

vocabulary.note: No word list is kept here; the executable tables are the source. This spec cites their version/hash; test_language_scope checks the hash.

rules.R1: speed word directly followed by a stage word (optional 地/一点/一些/点 between) -> that stage only; used in the context of the whole request, it never overrides negation, a conflict, or an explicit global request
rules.R2: stage word, optionally one of 入/到/进/下/上, optionally 得 or 时/的时候 (optionally followed by 要/用/采用/使用/保持/改用/改为/改成), then the speed word -> that stage only; the connective may be empty ('放入慢一点' is local to place); if R1 and R2 name different stages for one speed word the scope is undetermined
rules.R3: global ONLY with an explicit global cue in the same clause part (整个过程/全程/整体/...); the former branch 'no stage word -> global' is deleted. No dialogue context exists in this system, so context-given globals are not supported
rules.R4: scope cannot be reliably determined by the rules (no stage word and no global cue / stage word not linked / several stages possible / negation / stage without a speed dimension) -> clarification, no plan. It states a limit of this system, not that the sentence is ambiguous in Chinese; a word the vocabulary does not cover is a parsing coverage gap and never evidence for a global request

request_level.global_then_local_exception: a global level can be overridden for a stage only by an explicit local clause carrying an exception cue (但/但是/不过/除了/唯独/唯有/其中); the model expresses it as disjoint bindings (global minus that stage, plus the stage alone) because the existing structural rule allows one binding per instance; an overlapping answer is rejected as invalid
request_level.conflict: two different levels for the same scope, or a local-vs-global difference without an exception cue, is a conflict; clause order never decides; uses the existing 'conflict' status; when the model also returns two bindings on one instance, the existing structural rule (one instance, one binding) is not allowed to hide the conflict; the plan builder keeps its conflicting_levels refusal
request_level.negation: a negated speed word is never turned into a level; the request is sent back for clarification (negation is not supported)
request_level.normal_level: normal is a speed level like any other; the plan keeps the neutral value (the stage object is untouched). The neutral value is an execution default, not a user-specified speed

global_scope_definition: all stage instances of the registered program that support speed (T5: approach, descend, lift, transport, place, retreat); grasp has no speed dimension
level_values: shared LEVEL_RANGES defaults: slow v_max 0.06 m/s with w_max = min(3.0, v/0.12) = 0.5; normal untouched (0.12 m/s, 1.0 rad/s)
